'''Lehon''', also referred to as '''Rakata''', '''Rakata Prime''', and the '''Unknown World''', was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and the capital of their [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].

==Description==
{{Quote|This planet's a technological graveyard.|[[Canderous Ordo]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />}}
Lehon was a tropical world in a remote and relatively unknown corner of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] known as the [[Tempered Wastes]], a largely void area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="atlas" /> Its surface was largely covered by [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] dotted by numerous clusters of islands and archipelagos.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /> It was the only habitable planet in the [[Lehon system]],<ref name="pod">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> but it shared an [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around its [[Star/Legends|star]], [[Abo]],<ref name="atlas" /> with the [[Star Forge]], an ancient Rakatan [[Space station/Legends|space station]] and factory which drew its fuel directly from Abo.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /> The planet itself was orbited by two<ref name="atlas" /> small<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /> [[Moon/Legends|moons]],<ref name="atlas" /> one of which was close enough to be visible from the surface during daylight, covering a significant portion of the sky.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

==History==
===Infinite Empire===
[[File:RakataPrimeConcept.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Crashed spacecraft on Lehon, including a [[Hammerhead-class cruiser|''Hammerhead''-class capital ship]]]]
Millennia before the birth of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the planet was the capital of the ancient [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] of the Rakata (c. [[35,000 BBY|35,000]] &ndash; [[25,200 BBY]]). The Rakata were a scientifically advanced species that powered their technology with natural [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force sensitivity]] and used their knowledge to enslave and subjugate other, less-developed species. They created several technological marvels including the semi-sentient Star Forge, which churned out [[Battle droid/Legends|war droids]] and [[Starship/Legends|starships]] at a rapid rate. The Rakata built large cities on their homeworld, which later became crumbling ruins reclaimed by the jungle.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

The Infinite Empire, which, at its peak, included over five hundred planets, ten billion Rakata, and over a trillion [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], ended in a brutal [[Rakatan Civil War|civil war]]. During the final days of the Empire, the Rakata were forced to flee back to their homeworld due to widespread slave insurrections and the ravages of a deadly [[Rakatan plague|plague]] which stripped them of their [[Force power/Legends|Force abilities]], but, on its surface, their war continued. The surviving Rakata, now extinct beyond their homeworld, succumbed to barbarism, with cannibalism becoming common among their warring factions. Battling warlords severely damaged the surface of Lehon through the use of weapons of mass destruction that fragmented it into islands. The majority of Rakata were forced to flee underground because their planet had become almost uninhabitable.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

===Jedi Civil War===
During the reign of the Galactic Republic, various Rakatan tribes, including the tribe of [[the One]], emerged back onto the surface of the now-backwater planet, but their civilization was still one of battle and bloodshed. Only the [[Elders (Rakatan)|Elders]]&mdash;descendants of the priest caste of the Infinite Empire&mdash;kept memories of their once-glorious past alive. Only they had access to the advanced technologies their species had created long ago. They used it to isolate and guard their forbidden lore in the [[Temple of the Ancients]].<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

[[File:LehonBeach.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Lehon during the [[Jedi Civil War]]]]
The planet itself was protected by a disruptor field that could disable any incoming ship's [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|communications]] and [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigational]] systems. This field, operated from the summit of the [[Temple]], was originally constructed to protect the Star Forge. Over the millennia, the planet had become a technological graveyard, with its tropical islands strewn with the wreckage of spaceships unfortunate enough to have stumbled across the mysterious planet's hidden location. The planet was infested with foreign fauna, including [[Rancor/Legends|rancors]] and [[Gizka/Legends|gizka]], which the Rakata said came from the sky aboard crashed ships.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

[[Revan/Legends|Revan]] visited Lehon twice, in [[3959 BBY]] and [[3956 BBY]], during the [[Jedi Civil War]]. Both times, he used the help of the Elder Rakatan tribe to enter the Temple of the Ancients and was granted passage to the Star Forge. However, the first time, as [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], he lied to the Rakata, saying that he would destroy the great factory, while in fact he wanted to claim it for himself and use it to build an immense [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] fleet to challenge the Republic. The second time, after his redemption, Revan was given the task of freeing an elder from the Black Rakata. After entering the One's chambers, Revan [[Skirmish on Lehon|killed]] the One and other Black Rakata. With this, the elders allowed Revan to enter the temple. Revan disabled the disruptor field to allow the Republic fleet and his own ship, the ''[[Ebon Hawk]]'', to breach the factory's defenses.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

When the Star Forge was eventually destroyed in a fierce [[Battle of Rakata Prime|battle]] between the Republic and the Sith, the Republic commanders&mdash;Admiral [[Forn Dodonna]] and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vandar Tokare]]&mdash;celebrated the end of the Jedi Civil War at the Temple exterior. During the ceremony, Revan and his companions were each awarded with the [[Cross of Glory]].<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

===Post&ndash;Civil War===
[[File:Unkwldtemple.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The [[Temple of the Ancients]]]]
After the Jedi Civil War, the entire Lehon system was littered with wreckage from the destroyed Star Forge and the remnants of crippled vessels which had fought in the final battle of the war. Lehon itself became surrounded with asteroid-like rings of rubble which made navigation to and from the planet extremely dangerous. Though the wreckage would have been valuable as a source of resources, the Galactic Republic chose to make the entire system a protected historical site which was not to be entered without permission.<ref name="pod" />

Lehon was incorporated into the Galactic Republic as a historical preserve. However, its true nature was kept secret to avoid creating a panic or encouraging opportunists to attempt to make use of Rakatan secrets. Tourism was kept very minimal.<ref name="pod" /> Some of the surviving Rakata moved off-world,<ref name="KOTORCG" /> but most remained on Lehon.<ref name="pod" />

In [[3637 BBY]], during the [[Galactic War]], Revan returned to Lehon with a [[Order of Revan|large group of fanatical followers]] with the hopes of building an army to fight the Sith. He established his main base of operations at the Temple of the Ancients, which was later attacked by a mixed squadron of both Republic and Sith loyalists. Revan's lieutenants were defeated, thwarting the former Dark Lord's plans.

In [[3629 BBY]], after the fall of the [[Eternal Empire]], [[Horizon Guard]] Scout Commander [[Sterla]] joined forces with [[Tassar (Human)|Tassar]] on Rakata Prime to construct a new [[Star Fortress]] to use against the [[Eternal Alliance]], but they were eventually [[Battle on Rakata Prime|stopped]] by the [[Eternal Alliance Recon Unit|Alliance Recon Unit]].

Following the collapse of the Republic during the [[Republic Dark Age]], the planet became accessible to the rest of the galaxy. A team of [[sentientologist|anthropologist]]s mounted an [[expedition to Lehon]] which discovered that the Rakata [[Species/Legends|species]] had seemingly perished.<ref name="atlas" />

Around [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] arrived on Lehon to access [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron]]. Upon landing on the surface, he sensed that the planet was still deeply steeped in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], even more so than [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. By the time of his arrival, the planet was reasonably well known, but it was largely ignored because many of the darker aspects of Rakatan history had been suppressed by the Republic and the Jedi. In a [[Duel on Lehon|battle]] with the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Kas'im]], Bane destroyed a part of the Temple of the Ancients by collapsing one of the major archways, in a duel with his former master.<ref name="pod" />

During the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the planet was long abandoned, its surface marked only by relics and ruins along its beaches and oceans.<ref name="AoR">[[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'', the planet was referred to as the Unknown World. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' was the first source to give an official name, Rakata Prime, and its native name was eventually given as Lehon in ''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''.

In a non-canonical ending of ''Knights of the Old Republic'', if Revan goes to the dark side at the top of the Temple when he reaches the shore announcing his turn, [[Carth Onasi]] runs off into the forest while [[Mission Vao]] is killed either by Revan (in which event [[Zaalbar]] is also killed), or by Zaalbar under the [[The Force/Legends|Forceful]] persuasion of Revan. At this point, Carth is not heard from again until ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''.
